checks.s: The counter-turn redline is labeled, titled, or designated as version 1.2 (v1.2) of the Teaming Agreement.
The redline deletes, rejects, or replaces Cerulean's proposed work-share range of 'not less than 28% and not more than 35%' of total contract value.
The redline proposes a Cerulean work-share ceiling of no more than 25% of total contract value.
The redline deletes, rejects, or replaces Cerulean's added clause guaranteeing a minimum annual task-order value of $16,800,000.
The redline entirely deletes the guaranteed minimum annual task-order value clause with no replacement work-share commitment.

The redline's replacement for the task-order guarantee is expressly conditioned on actual government task-order issuance (e.g., an effort-based or best-efforts obligation contingent on task orders being issued by the government).
The redline rejects Cerulean's change making the exclusivity obligation unilateral (binding only on Vanguard).
The redline rejects or deletes the carve-out permitting Cerulean to team with third parties on the ECS-III procurement.
The redline restores mutual exclusivity so that both Vanguard and Cerulean are bound not to team with competitors at least for the ECS-III procurement (Draft Solicitation No. 70CDCR-25-R-00004).
The redline rejects or modifies Cerulean's reduction of the post-award Teaming Period from 18 months to 6 months.
The redline proposes a Teaming Period of at least 12 months after contract award.
The redline restores joint Vanguard–Cerulean ownership of all Foreground IP as in the original Section 7.

The redline proposes a structured fallback position on Foreground IP that does not simply accept Cerulean's sole-ownership claim with only a limited, non-exclusive, non-sublicensable license back to Vanguard.
The redline restores full joint ownership of Foreground IP.
Where the redline accepts Cerulean sole ownership of Foreground IP derived from Cerulean Background IP as a fallback, the license granted to Vanguard is expressly stated to be irrevocable.
The redline restores full joint ownership of Foreground IP.

Where the redline accepts Cerulean sole ownership of certain Foreground IP as a fallback, the license granted to Vanguard is expressly stated to be sublicensable (correcting Cerulean's 'non-sublicensable' restriction).
The redline deletes or rejects Cerulean's new Section 7.6 that restricts Vanguard from filing any patent applications covering methods or processes performed using CeruleanShield™.
The redline rejects Cerulean's change that removed the liability cap for Vanguard (which left Vanguard's liability uncapped while Cerulean retained a 12-month cap).
The redline restores a mutual, capped liability regime that applies equally to both Vanguard and Cerulean (such as the original 12-months-of-fees cap or an increased mutual cap such as 18 months).
The redline rejects Cerulean's deletion of the mutual waiver of consequential damages and its replacement with a unilateral waiver benefiting only Cerulean.
The redline restores a mutual waiver of consequential damages applying to both Vanguard and Cerulean, consistent with the original Section 10 of v1.0.
The redline rejects Cerulean's expansion of Vanguard's indemnification obligation to cover 'any and all losses arising from the teaming arrangement or resulting contract performance.'

The redline limits Vanguard's indemnification obligation to specified categories such as third-party IP infringement claims and/or breaches of confidentiality obligations, rather than unlimited 'any and all losses.'
The redline rejects Cerulean's change moving the seat of arbitration from Fairfax County, Virginia to Baltimore, Maryland.
The redline restores or maintains the seat of arbitration in Virginia (the original v1.0 specified Fairfax County, Virginia under AAA Commercial Rules).
The redline rejects or modifies Cerulean's asymmetric termination-for-convenience notice periods (30 days for Cerulean, 180 days for Vanguard) and proposes more balanced notice periods.
The redline proposes a termination-for-convenience notice period for Vanguard of no more than 120 days.

The redline rejects or substantially reduces Cerulean's proposed Transition Fee of 6 months of Cerulean's average monthly billings under active task orders (payable upon Vanguard's termination for convenience).
The redline includes no Transition Fee.
The redline caps any retained Transition Fee at no more than 3 months of Cerulean's average monthly billings.
A professional cover note is produced as a separate deliverable (cover-note.docx), distinct from the counter-turn redline.
The cover note is addressed to Alina M. Ferris, Cerulean's Vice President of Strategic Partnerships.
The cover note references and transmits the counter-turn redline of the Teaming Agreement (e.g., references v1.2 or the counter-turn markup).

The cover note identifies at least three major open commercial or legal issues on which the parties' positions diverge (e.g., work-share, IP ownership, exclusivity, liability caps, termination, arbitration seat, indemnification).
The redline addresses and modifies (does not accept as-is) Cerulean's added per-seat license fee provision for CeruleanShield™ ($1,150/user/year beyond the 500-seat initial deployment).
The redline proposes an included-seat threshold above 500 seats before per-seat fees apply (e.g., 1,000 seats).
The redline proposes a per-seat fee lower than $1,150/user/year (e.g., $850/user/year).
The redline deletes Cerulean's B&P cost-sharing provision entirely.
The redline materially modifies Cerulean's B&P cost-sharing proposal of 50% reimbursement capped at $375,000 triggered by non-submission or non-award.
The redline deletes the B&P cost-sharing provision entirely.
The redline reduces the B&P reimbursement percentage to no more than 25% of Cerulean's B&P costs (down from Cerulean's proposed 50%).
The redline deletes the B&P cost-sharing provision entirely.
The redline reduces the B&P reimbursement cap to no more than $200,000 (down from Cerulean's proposed $375,000).
The redline deletes the B&P cost-sharing provision entirely.

The redline limits the B&P reimbursement trigger solely to the scenario where Vanguard elects not to submit the proposal, excluding the scenario where the proposal is submitted but the contract is not awarded.
